title: Google Launches Gemini 3.6 Flash and Teases Gemini 4 as Flagship Pro Model Remains Delayed
excerpt: Alphabet releases three new lightweight AI models but offers no timeline for Gemini 3.5 Pro, the top-tier model Wall Street is watching ahead of Wednesday’s earnings call.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Google launched Gemini 3.6 Flash and Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, plus a cybersecurity model.
  • The flagship Gemini 3.5 Pro model is delayed due to unmet internal coding benchmarks.
  • Training for Gemini 4 has begun, indicating future AI advancements.
  • CEO Sundar Pichai will address the Pro delay during Alphabet's Q2 earnings call.
  • Competitors like Anthropic and OpenAI have released new models, increasing market pressure.

  • Google released Gemini 3.6 Flash and Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite on Tuesday, along with a new cybersecurity-focused model called Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber
  • The flagship Gemini 3.5 Pro model, originally slated for June, remains delayed due to the model reportedly falling short of internal coding benchmarks
  • Google confirmed that training has begun on Gemini 4, signaling the next major generation of its AI models
  • CEO Sundar Pichai faces questions on the delay at Alphabet’s Q2 earnings call on Wednesday

Google released three new lightweight versions of its Gemini AI model on Tuesday, but shared no timeline for the flagship Gemini 3.5 Pro that investors and developers have been awaiting for weeks, according to Reuters.

The new lineup includes Gemini 3.6 Flash and Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, updated versions of Google’s cost-efficient models designed for use cases that don’t require cutting-edge capabilities. Google also unveiled Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber, a specialized variant tailored for cybersecurity applications.

The Pro Delay

All eyes remain on Gemini 3.5 Pro, the top-tier model that CEO Sundar Pichai originally promised for a June launch during his keynote at the Google I/O developer conference in May. The delay is reportedly due to the model falling short of internal goals, particularly in coding — which has emerged as a lucrative enterprise AI use case.

> **"Anthropic rolled out its Mythos 5 and Fable 5 models, which the U.S."** https://x.com/Google/status/2079589757395312767

Google said Gemini 3.5 Pro is being tested with partners and would be coming “soon.” In one press release, the company also confirmed that training has commenced on Gemini 4, its next-generation model family.

Pichai is likely to face pointed questions about the Pro delay when Alphabet holds its second-quarter earnings conference call on Wednesday.

Competitive Pressure Mounts

Google’s rivals have not stood still. Anthropic rolled out its Mythos 5 and Fable 5 models, which the U.S. government deemed powerful enough to raise national security concerns. OpenAI launched GPT-5.6 earlier this month after a similar government-requested delay to vet security risks.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=rYosnjPRDQ4

“3.5 Flash delivers frontier-level intelligence at exceptional speed — proving you no longer have to trade quality for latency.”

— Google DeepMind

Google’s Gemini 3 model family, launched last November, had briefly returned the company to the front of the AI race and reportedly caused OpenAI to issue an internal “code red.” But the sustained delay of Gemini 3.5 Pro has allowed competitors to reclaim momentum.

The Flash Strategy

Google’s Flash models occupy a different niche. The Gemini 3.5 Flash, released in May, outperformed Google’s own Gemini 3.1 Pro on coding and agentic benchmarks while running four times faster and at roughly half the cost. DeepMind’s chief technologist Koray Kavukcuoglu said at I/O that Flash “offers an incredible combination of quality and low latency.”

The strategy reflects a bet on cost-per-useful-task rather than raw benchmark dominance. Pichai has claimed companies could save upwards of $1 billion per year by shifting most AI workloads to Gemini models.

Google DeepMind staff described the new Flash Cyber variant as “a cost-efficient and highly capable alternative to large, costly cybersecurity models.”

Earnings Test Ahead

Alphabet’s Q2 earnings call on Wednesday will be a critical moment. Investors are watching whether the Pro delay signals deeper technical challenges at DeepMind or a deliberate decision to prioritize safety and quality.

Google’s AI spending has been substantial, and the Gemini app has crossed 900 million monthly active users. The company’s distribution advantage — integrating Gemini across Search, Android, and its cloud platform — gives it scale that standalone labs cannot match. Whether that translates into enterprise revenue depends heavily on when and how Pro arrives.
